facts.statement: The genus Cruralispennia was formally described by Wang and colleagues in 2017.
facts.quote: authority: Wang et al., 2017

facts.statement: Cruralispennia lived during the Early Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Early Cretaceous,

facts.statement: The only known specimen of Cruralispennia was found in the Huajiying Formation in China.
facts.quote: The only known specimen of Cruralispennia was discovered in the Early Cretaceous Huajiying Formation of China

facts.statement: Cruralispennia lived approximately 130.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: approximately 130.7 million years ago

facts.statement: The genus name Cruralispennia means "shin feather" and the species name multidonta means "many-toothed".
facts.quote: The generic name is Latin for "shin feather", while the specific name means "many-toothed".

facts.statement: The holotype specimen is a semi-articulated partial skeleton surrounded by carbonized feathers.
facts.quote: a semi-articulated partial skeleton surrounded by the remains of carbonized feathers

facts.statement: The left lower jaw of Cruralispennia preserves fourteen teeth, which is a high number for enantiornitheans.
facts.quote: The left dentary preserves fourteen teeth, a characteristically high number compared to other enantiornitheans

facts.statement: The pygostyle of Cruralispennia is short, broad, and tapers into an upturned tip.
facts.quote: The fused pygostyle of IVPP 21711 is characteristically short and broad, tapering distally into an upturned tip

facts.statement: Cruralispennia had a short forelimb with a robust humerus typical of enantiornitheans.
facts.quote: The forelimb is rather short, with a robust humerus possessing enantiornithean features

facts.statement: The claws on the toes of Cruralispennia were sharp and curved.
facts.quote: The toe claws are sharp and curved

facts.statement: The unique wire-like leg feathers, called PWFDT, were also found on the front edge of the left wing.
facts.quote: This form of feather morphology, dubbed "proximally wire-like part with a short filamentous distal tip (PWFDT)", is also present in feathers projecting along the front edge of the left wing

facts.statement: It is debated whether the unique leg feathers are a novel type or simply immature feathers formed after a recent molt.
facts.quote: Another possibility is that the PWFDT feathers are not a novel type of feather unique to Cruralispennia, but instead are immature pennaceous feathers formed after a recent molt

facts.statement: The unique PWFDT feather morphology is currently known only in Cruralispennia.
facts.quote: PWFDT feathers are currently only known in Cruralispennia

facts.statement: Melanosomes in the leg feathers had the shortest aspect ratio, suggesting a dark brown coloration.
facts.quote: A sample taken from the crural feathers had eumelanosomes with the shortest aspect ratio, which may have corresponded to dark brown coloration

facts.statement: High aspect ratio melanosomes in Cruralispennia feathers may correlate with glossy or iridescent colors.
facts.quote: High aspect ratios have been known to correlate with glossy or iridescent colors

facts.statement: Cruralispennia is classified within Enantiornithes based on humerus features, lack of procoracoid processes, and a long scapular acromion.
facts.quote: Cruralispennia was referred to Enantiornithes in the taxon's description due to various features of the humerus, a lack of procoracoid processes, and a long acromion process of the scapula

facts.statement: The early appearance of this derived genus suggests the evolutionary history of ornithothoraces is older than previously indicated by fossils.
facts.quote: the presence of such a derived genus so early in the Cretaceous is evidence that the family tree of ornithothoraces is older than currently known fossils suggest

facts.statement: The holotype fossil of Cruralispennia is cataloged as IVPP 21711 and is housed at the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology.
facts.quote: Los restos fósiles fueron catalogados como IVPP 21711 y son alojados en el Instituto de Paleontología de Vertebrados y Paleoantropología

facts.statement: The only known species, Cruralispennia multidonta, lived during the Early Cretaceous Barremian stage, approximately 130.7 million years ago, in the Huanjiying Formation of Hebei province, China.
facts.quote: La especie tipo y única conocida es Cruralispennia multidonta, cuyos restos fósiles se encontraron la Formación Huanjiying en la cuenca de Sichakou, en la provincia de Hebei al noreste de China, la cual data de hace 130,7 millones de años, durante la época del Barremiense del Cretácico

facts.statement: Cruralispennia is an extinct genus of enantiornithine bird.
facts.quote: Cruralispennia es un género extinto de ave enantiornite

facts.statement: The premaxilla of Cruralispennia is short, forms a 43° angle with the frontal bone, and preserves two teeth.
facts.quote: El premaxilar es corto, y forma un ángulo de 43° con respecto al frontal, y preserva dos dientes

facts.statement: Cruralispennia is distinguished from other enantiornithines by having 14 teeth in the dentary.
facts.quote: Se distingue de otras enantiornitas por tener 14 dientes en el dentario

facts.statement: Cruralispennia possessed a short plow-shaped pygostyle, a feature generally associated with more derived birds in the Ornithuromorpha group.
facts.quote: un pigóstilo corto en forma de arado (un rasgo generalmente asociado con las aves más derivadas del grupo Ornithuromorpha)

facts.statement: The sternum of Cruralispennia has a V-shaped posterior margin and two pairs of trabeculae.
facts.quote: el esternón tiene un margen caudal en forma de letra V y dos pares de trabéculos

facts.statement: A histological study of the humerus of specimen IVPP 21711 found no lines of arrested growth, indicating the individual died within a single season.
facts.quote: A histological study of IVPP 21711's humerus found no lines of arrested growth present within the bone. This is evidence that IVPP 21711 died within one season.

facts.statement: Evidence suggests that individuals of Cruralispennia grew rapidly, reaching adult size in less than one year.
facts.quote: These factors are support for the idea that individuals of Cruralispennia grew quickly, reaching adult size in less than a year.

facts.statement: Cruralispennia's rapid growth strategy contrasts with other enantiornithines, which are believed to have taken several years to reach adulthood.
facts.quote: This is in contrast with other enantiornitheans, which are believed to have grown slowly, taking several years to reach adulthood.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that the crural PWFDT feathers of Cruralispennia may have functioned in insulation, heat shielding, or social signaling.
facts.quote: Some of these possible functions include insulation, heat shielding, or social signalling.

facts.statement: The narrow crural PWFDT feathers of Cruralispennia were likely too simple for aerodynamic use but narrow enough not to hinder flight.
facts.quote: Although PWFDT feathers were probably too simple to provide any aerodynamic advantage, their narrowness means that they were unlikely to have been an inhibiting factor either.

facts.statement: The genus Cruralispennia lived during the Hauterivian stage, from 132.6 to 125.77 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Hauterivian to Hauterivian (132.6 to 125.77 million years ago)

facts.statement: It is debated whether the early diversification of enantiornithines seen in Cruralispennia reflects a high evolutionary rate or is an artifact of poor sampling immediately after the Jurassic.
facts.quote: lo cual indica que ya hacía 130 millones de años las aves de este grupo se habían diversificado en varios linajes, lo que indica que hubo una alta tasa evolutiva en el plano corporal de las aves a principios del Cretácico, a menos que se deba a un efecto del escaso muestreo de aves justo después del Jurásico
